subject: Catalyst Health — Redwood eval playbook & dataset/score criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.p@catalysthealth.com>, Samir Kumar <samir.kumar@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Catalysts call recap + next steps for Redwood eval

Hi Aisha / Samir — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap (30-min discovery):
- Primary use case: Triage assistant to surface relevant clinical notes for nurses (categorization + short summary).
- Success metrics: precision on top-1 category, downstream triage time reduction, and reduction in human review load.
- Data: you have ~180k historical triage items; for evaluation you suggested a 5–10k de-identified sample.

Redwood recommended evaluation approach (short):
- Models we recommend to test initially: rw-13b-instruct-q4 (strong instruction-following baseline), rw-7b-refine (faster, cheaper baseline), and an Llama-3-13B family variant you already referenced.
- Evaluation flavors: categorical classification (primary label), summary quality (ROUGE-L + manual QA), and hallucination check (label-level hallucination flag).
- Minimum sample guidance: 5k stratified by label to get stable precision/F1 estimates; for early smoke tests 1k balanced sample is OK.

What I’m attaching / sharing:
- redwood-eval-template.md (attached) — evaluation template we usually run; includes prompt bank, scoring rubric, and example CSV schema.
- catalyst_sample_subset.csv (attached) — a 250-row sample we discussed (anonymized).
- Drive folder with full prompt bank + scoring rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CatalystEval

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm how you’ll share the full 5k sample (S3 bucket, secure Drive link, or we can provision a short-lived Redwood ingestion endpoint).
2) Confirm any PII/anonymization constraints we should enforce (we can redact PHI on ingest if needed).
3) If you want us to run the evaluation on Redwood Private (your VPC) vs our hosted cluster — tell us preference and we’ll prepare an ops plan.

Next steps (proposal):
- If you give us the 5k sample and sign the attached SOW/NDA, we’ll spin up a dedicated eval run and deliver a comparison report (model metrics, prompt variants, and ops notes) in ~7 business days.

I’ve copied Marissa (our product lead) and Jordan (solutions engineer) to help with ops and fast onboarding. Happy to jump on a short follow-up if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Anonymization: our legal team requires that any PHI be removed or tokenized before leaving our environment. We can provide a redacted dump to your ingestion endpoint, or we can share an S3 bucket in our account and give Redwood a role to read (preferred).
- Sample size: we can start with 2k stratified sample for the first run and expand to 5k if the initial results look promising.
- Security: we need details on how Redwood handles ephemeral credentials and logs for evaluation runs (we flagged this as a must-have in the procurement checklist).

Also, Samir is attaching the countersigned NDA and a short note from procurement about billing contacts. Can you confirm whether an evaluation on Redwood hosted implies sending data outside our AWS account?

Best,
Aisha

aisha.p@catalysthealth.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalysts call recap + next steps for Redwood eval

Hi Aisha / Samir — great questions, answering inline below.

On anonymization / data residency:
- If you prefer to keep data in your AWS account we can run the eval in two ways: (1) Redwood Private on your VPC (we deploy our evaluation runner inside your account), or (2) a one-time cross-account S3 read-role where our hosted runner pulls the sample into an encrypted bucket we control for the duration of the job and deletes after results are delivered. For initial trials the cross-account S3 role is the fastest; Private is recommended for long-term/production evaluation.

On credentials & logs:
- We issue short-lived IAM roles (assume-role) scoped to a single S3 prefix and a single job. Logs are visible in the Redwood Console and can be forwarded to your logging endpoint or to your CloudWatch for audit retention. We support KMS key wrapping so your data is encrypted with your key while at rest.

On hosted vs private:
- Hosted eval runs do mean data will briefly be staged in our environment if you choose cross-account S3 transfer; we’ll provide the job manifest and you can revoke the role immediately after ingestion. If you need zero-data-exfiltration, Redwood Private (VPC deployment) is the right path.

Evaluation specifics (ops & scoring):
- CSV schema we prefer: id,text,label,created_at,source (see redwood-eval-template.md). Please avoid nested JSON fields in the csv; separate annotations in a separate file if needed.
- Sample sizes suggested: 1k (smoke), 2–5k (stable run), 10k+ (stress & stratified analysis).
- Core metrics we’ll report: top-1 accuracy, macro F1 by label, confusion matrix, per-label precision & recall, ROUGE-L for summaries, and an explicit hallucination rate defined as model output with contradicted facts vs record-level evidence.
- Statistical significance: we’ll include bootstrap CIs on F1/accuracy and flag regressed prompts if delta > 3 percentage points with p<0.05.

Ops timeline for a 2k run:
Day 0: we get sample + countersigned NDA (done)
Day 1: Jordan and team ingest, sanity-check sample schema (1 business day)
Day 2–3: run baseline models (rw-7b-refine, rw-13b-instruct-q4) + prompt variants
Day 4–5: manual QA on 200 triage items for summary quality and hallucination sampling
Day 6–7: deliver report and recommendations + ops notes for production rollout

Security doc links: https://app.redwood.ai/security (we’ll add a short SSO/SOC2 excerpt to the Drive folder).

Action here: can you grant redwood-eval@redwood.ai an s3:ListBucket/GetObject role scoped to s3://catalyst-health-eval/2k-run? If not, we’ll send a pre-signed upload endpoint.

Jordan will reach out to coordinate the actual ingestion job. Thanks again.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
